title: Soft-Body Collision Arena with Momentum Transfer
description: Two characters stand on a deformable soft-body terrain grid. The user launches jelly-like projectiles at CesiumMan and Soldier, causing soft-body deformations on impact that propagate across the mesh surface. Players must manage momentum conservation between characters by linking them with elastic tethers, adjusting stiffness and damping, and using undo/redo to refine their deformation sculpture.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load CesiumMan.glb and soldier.glb, placing them 4 units apart on a 20x20 subdivided plane mesh (60x60 segments) that acts as a soft-body terrain using a spring-mass simulation. Each vertex has position, velocity, and is connected to neighbors with spring forces. Gravity pulls vertices down, a ground plane constraint prevents infinite sag, and structural plus shear springs maintain shape. Place CesiumMan at (-2,0,0) and Soldier at (2,0,0) on the terrain surface. Interactions (10-14 steps total): (1) Left-click on the terrain to launch a sphere projectile from the camera toward the click point. On impact, apply a radial impulse to nearby terrain vertices creating a soft-body crater that ripples outward. (2) Right-click drag between the two characters to create an elastic tether visualized as a line; momentum transfers through the tether so deforming terrain near one character tugs the other's local terrain region. (3) A slider panel controls spring stiffness (0.1-2.0) and damping (0.01-0.5) globally. (4) A mass slider (0.5-3.0) adjusts projectile mass, affecting crater depth via momentum conservation (p=mv). (5) Press 'T' to toggle tether on/off. (6) Ctrl+Z for undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z for redo, storing up to 20 snapshots of all vertex positions. (7) Press 'R' to reset terrain to flat. (8) Press 'F' to freeze/unfreeze simulation. Display a HUD showing total system momentum magnitude, projectile count, and current spring parameters. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,10,15) looking at origin, DirectionalLight from (5,10,7) with intensity 1.5, AmbientLight at 0.4, and a subtle grid helper beneath the terrain. Color the terrain mesh using a MeshPhongMaterial with vertex colors mapped to displacement magnitude (green=rest, red=deep deformation). Animate both GLB models with their default animations. The soft-body simulation runs each frame with 4 substeps for stability.
